patch_description: Crossover of the best-performing variants. The key insight from the two lowest-cost programs is building a single shared Steiner-style multicast tree (759.09 vs 1026-1035 for naive/parallel-path approaches): each tree edge carries data once instead of once per (partition, dst), eliminating redundant shared-prefix transfers. The hybrid keeps the efficient one-shot tree construction (built once, reversed-graph Dijkstra cached outside the loop), adds a robust per-dst fallback to direct Dijkstra paths for unreachable destinations, and reuses the tree across all partitions. This preserves the exact I/O contract while minimizing cost.
